subject: home-office-rent-share
title: Home office share of rent
decision: Claim 40% of the rent for the home office; every other cost Umar pays personally for the business at 100%.
rationale: The rule in CLAUDE.md and the draft Director Resolution, which gave a $24,143.25 reimbursement for 2025.

subject: home-office-rent-share
title: Home office share of rent
decision: Claim 30% of the rent. For 2025 that is 30% of $31,116 = $9,335, the rent line on the filed T2 2025. In 2026 it is $780 a month, $789 from 15 September.
rationale: Easier to defend: CRA has no fixed percentage and the share must match the office's floor area or room count. Umar confirmed 30% again on 23 September 2026. Keep a floor plan, photos and the lease to back it.
sources: 2025/Corporate/accountant files/final/1. T2 Yr '25 - Client Copy - 15248132 CANADA INC (20251231) - Umar Farooq Aslam.pdf

subject: mercedes-business-use
title: Mercedes business use
decision: The filed T2 2025 deducts all Mercedes costs at 100% business use, including the whole lease ($12,000.04 in 2025).
rationale: The card ledger and the accountant treated the car as fully business. No mileage log supported it.
sources: 2025/Corporate/accountant files/final/1. T2 Yr '25 - Client Copy - 15248132 CANADA INC (20251231) - Umar Farooq Aslam.pdf

subject: mercedes-business-use
title: Mercedes business use
decision: Umar states business use at about 95%.
rationale: Owner's estimate for insurance and compliance notes; no log, and both insurance certificates say personal use.

subject: mercedes-business-use
title: Mercedes business use
decision: The HST package sent to Saira claims the Mercedes at 100% business use.
rationale: Umar's instruction during the package build; the dashboard checklist moved from 95% to 100% to match the email.

subject: mercedes-business-use
title: Mercedes business use
decision: Claim the Mercedes at 80% business use from 27 September 2025, plus the s.67.3 lease cap. Use 80% on the T2 2026 too so the returns agree. No credit for car costs from 15 August to 26 September 2025, when Umar drove his own car and was paid mileage.
rationale: 100% gave HST credits of $5,372.45, well above last year's $3,900.43. Umar's 2025 mileage logs on his own car point to about 52%, his own estimate to 95%; 80% sits between. Claude warned there is still no log. Umar asked about 85% on 7 October but has not decided; 80% stands.

subject: payments-to-umar-2025
title: What the $28,000 paid to Umar in 2025 was
decision: The four transfers to Umar from January to April 2025 ($6,000, $7,000, $7,000, $8,000) are recorded as 'Dividends to Umar', like the 2023 and 2024 transfers.
rationale: The bank workbook's original caption.

subject: payments-to-umar-2025
title: What the $28,000 paid to Umar in 2025 was
decision: Not dividends: $24,143.25 repays business costs Umar paid on his own cards (rent at 40%), and $3,856.75 is an advance he must repay by 31 December 2026 under s.15(2).
rationale: Draft Director Resolution dated 31 December 2025, never signed.

subject: payments-to-umar-2025
title: What the $28,000 paid to Umar in 2025 was
decision: At 30% rent the split becomes $21,031.65 reimbursement and a $6,968.35 advance, still due back by 31 December 2026.
rationale: Followed from cutting the rent share to 30%. Never adopted in the filed return.

subject: payments-to-umar-2025
title: What the $28,000 paid to Umar in 2025 was
decision: As filed, there is no advance and no loan. The T2 2025 treats $41,357 of Umar's personally paid business costs as expenses: the $28,000 repaid plus $13,357 the corporation still owes him (Schedule 100 line 2780). Future payments to Umar are labelled expense reimbursement.
rationale: The accountant spread the amounts across rent, vehicle, phone, insurance and other expenses. Umar confirmed on 3 August 2026 that no shareholder loan remains, so there is no repayment deadline.
sources: 2025/Corporate/accountant files/final/1. T2 Yr '25 - Client Copy - 15248132 CANADA INC (20251231) - Umar Farooq Aslam.pdf

subject: no-t5-2025
title: No T5 slip for 2025
decision: The corporation issues no T5 for 2025 because it paid no dividends in 2025.
rationale: The $28,000 to Umar is expense reimbursement; the filed T2 2025 shows no 2025 dividends.
sources: 2025/Corporate/accountant files/final/1. T2 Yr '25 - Client Copy - 15248132 CANADA INC (20251231) - Umar Farooq Aslam.pdf

subject: zeeshan-no-t4a-nr4
title: No T4A or NR4 for Zeeshan
decision: No T4A, no NR4 and no Reg. 105 withholding for Zeeshan, the offshore subcontractor paid through WISE.
rationale: He works entirely outside Canada (Pakistan), so his pay is not Canadian source income. Keep the contractor agreement and WISE records.

subject: oct-10-2025-refund
title: What the 10 October 2025 CRA deposit was
decision: The $4,960.50 received on 10 October 2025 is a corporate tax refund, partly from overpaid 2025 instalments ($2,108).
rationale: CLAUDE.md and the 2025 dashboard; the workbook row was labelled 'Corp tax (2025)'.

subject: oct-10-2025-refund
title: What the 10 October 2025 CRA deposit was
decision: It is the refund of the HST overpaid on 15 September 2025. Not revenue and not corporate tax.
rationale: Payments toward the 2024 to 2025 HST year total $40,082 against $35,121.50 owed, exactly $4,960.50 over. The October 2025 bank statement shows the deposit as 'CANADA GST/TPS'.

subject: corp-tax-instalments-2026
title: How 2026 corporate tax instalments are paid
decision: Pay 2026 instalments on an estimate of 2026 tax, about $900 a month, instead of CRA's schedule ($4,011 on 31 May then $1,337 a month, $13,370 in all).
rationale: Allowed by s.157; interest only arises if 2026 tax ends up above the instalments. Recheck in November: the September projection is $14,665 of tax against $10,500 of instalments.

subject: accountant
title: Who the accountant is
decision: Saira (CPACM) prepares the corporation's returns: the T2 for 2023 and 2024, the HST returns and the 2025 bookkeeping to 14 August.
rationale: Her fees: $904 in January 2024, $1,073.50 in February 2025 and invoice 2041 for $423.75.

subject: accountant
title: Who the accountant is
decision: Ejaz Pirwani (Fintax Associate) prepares the 2025 personal returns for Umar and Maham and then the T2 2025.
rationale: He transmitted the T1s signed on 20 April 2026 and the T2 filed on 18 May 2026; fee $1,440.75 paid 21 May.
sources: 2025/Corporate/accountant files/final/1. T2 Yr '25 - Client Copy - 15248132 CANADA INC (20251231) - Umar Farooq Aslam.pdf

subject: accountant
title: Who the accountant is
decision: Back to Saira (CPACM) from September 2026: she files the HST return for 2025 to 2026 and prepares the T2 2026.
rationale: Umar stopped working with Ejaz Pirwani.

subject: previous-accountant-not-named
title: Keep the previous accountant out of Saira's papers
decision: In anything for Saira, refer to Ejaz Pirwani only as 'the previous accountant' and leave his $1,440.75 invoice out of her package. Its $165.75 HST credit is still claimed.
rationale: Umar's instruction. The T2 2025 client copy goes in unaltered, preparer box included.

subject: hst-lease-itc
title: HST credit on the Mercedes lease
decision: Claim all HST paid on the lease in the 2025 to 2026 return: $2,789.85 ($776.55 at signing plus 10 x $201.33).
rationale: Umar asked to claim it in full and leave the s.67.3 cap as a question for Saira. Earlier the same day the capped version gave a $2,868.95 refund; the full claim gave $4,400.05.

subject: hst-lease-itc
title: HST credit on the Mercedes lease
decision: Claim 35.94% of the lease HST: 80% business use times the 44.93% cap = $1,002.69.
rationale: Follows the move to 80% business use. Line 106 becomes $3,377.06 and the refund $2,404.66.

subject: lease-cap-list-price
title: Price used for the lease cap
decision: Work the s.67.3 cap on a $99,500 list price: $38,000 / (85% x $99,500) = 44.93% of each lease payment counts.
rationale: Using the full $109,929.95 list including options gives 40.67%. Which one applies is a question for Saira.
sources: 2026/Corporate/HST Filing 2025-26 - for Saira/05 Vehicle lease - Mercedes GLC 43/lease-pricing-worksheet.pdf

subject: hospital-and-parking-charges
title: Hospital and parking charges on the corporate card
decision: Credit Valley Hospital charges of 27 July 2026 ($1,200 plus $21) are personal: no HST credit, and they reduce what the corporation owes Umar. Halton Health Care parking in October and November 2025 ($78.25) is business and claimed.
rationale: Umar said hospital charges went on the corporate card by mistake, then clarified that only Credit Valley is personal.

subject: ifly-calgary
title: iFly Calgary charge
decision: Treat the $319.76 iFly Calgary charge of 11 July 2026 as client entertainment at 50%: HST credit $18.40.
rationale: Umar said it was client entertainment. HST_RETURN notes still showed it as travel ($36.79), so Saira should confirm.

subject: vault-routing
title: Where tax notes are saved
decision: Tax notes go only in the obsidian-me vault under personal/taxes, never in obsidian-dev.
rationale: Umar's instruction after a save wrote tax lessons to the dev vault; that commit was reverted.

subject: saira-package-scope
title: What the next package for Saira covers
decision: The next spreadsheet for Saira covers every corporate transaction from 1 January to 31 December 2026, for the T2 2026. Build it after the December statements arrive, with the Mercedes at 80% and rent at 30%.
rationale: Saira asked for the whole calendar year for the corporate return, not another HST year workpaper.

subject: saira-applies-80-percent
title: Who updates the HST workpaper
decision: Do not send Saira the revised workpaper; she applies 80% and the cap to her own copy. Compare her figures line by line when they arrive.
rationale: Umar had already told her. She says her books show more than ours.

subject: opening-retained-earnings-2025
title: Retained earnings at the start of 2025
decision: Start 2025 with retained earnings of $57,377, the T2 2024 closing figure, not the $129,924 on the previous accountant's August 2025 sheet.
rationale: Her figure added the $72,550 of 2024 dividends back in. The filed T2 2025 uses $57,377.
sources: 2025/Corporate/accountant files/final/1. T2 Yr '25 - Client Copy - 15248132 CANADA INC (20251231) - Umar Farooq Aslam.pdf

subject: hst-2024-25-final
title: HST return for 2024 to 2025 stays as filed

subject: equipment-expensed-2025
title: 2025 equipment written off at once
decision: Expense the 2025 equipment purchases (about $13,983, including the Mac Studio) in full under computer related costs instead of depreciating them.
rationale: Umar's choice. The risk is timing only: CRA could make the corporation spread them out (computers at 55% a year, furniture at 20%).

subject: small-business-rate

decision: Claim the small business deduction: combined rate 12.2% (9% federal plus 3.2% Ontario).
rationale: The corporation is far below the $500,000 limit. The accountant's first draft used about 15%; the revised file brought tax down from $15,989 to $13,368.

decision: Accept the accountant's treatment of equipment, WISE fees inside subcontracts, software inside business taxes and the director account, without raising them.

subject: pool-lab-and-tcx

subject: hst-sales-timing
title: When a sale counts for HST
decision: Count sales by the date the money arrives, as Saira did for 2024 to 2025.
rationale: The deposits at each end of the year (22 August 2025 and 21 August 2026) are both $8,542.80, so invoice date would give the same total.

subject: hst-exclusions
title: What is left out of the 2025 to 2026 HST return
decision: Leave out the two CRA deposits ($4,960.50 and $4,644.90), the $5,800 payment of 15 September 2025, the $1,221 hospital charge, US suppliers that charge no Canadian HST (Vercel, Anthropic, OpenAI, Z.AI), simplified registrants (Paddle), rent and insurance (exempt) and the 9 September 2025 fuel for Umar's own car.
rationale: None is taxable revenue or carries a claimable credit.

subject: phone-and-internet

rationale: Placeholder before the bills were loaded.

subject: phone-and-internet

title: How often Maham's payroll is remitted
decision: Remit quarterly as a small remitter: $1,380.42 on 15 July, 15 October and 15 January.

subject: payroll-remittance-frequency
title: How often Maham's payroll is remitted
decision: Remit monthly, $460.14 in nine scheduled payments, the last on 31 December 2026.

subject: maham-2026-pay
title: Maham's 2026 pay
decision: Pay Maham $24,000 gross for April to December 2026: nine monthly payments of $2,666.67, $2,347.84 after deductions. CPP applies; EI does not, because she is the owner's spouse.
rationale: Replaces an earlier plan of $2,000 a month for twelve months. Withholding is trued up over the nine months ($177.52 a month); a more cautious method ($269.07 a month) is open for the accountant.

subject: transfers-and-refunds
title: Investment transfers and CRA refunds
decision: Transfers to Wealthsimple ($55,000 by 31 August 2026) are moves between the corporation's own accounts, not expenses. CRA refunds are not revenue.
rationale: Neither changes taxable income.

subject: director-reimbursement
title: Repaying Umar for business costs
decision: Repaying Umar for business costs he paid personally is not income to him: no T4, no benefit, no deadline. Track it as owed to Umar and count only 2026 items, since $4,491.32 of August to December 2025 items are already in the $13,357.
rationale: The corporation already deducted the costs when it recorded them.

subject: withdraw-reimbursement
title: Drawing what the corporation owes Umar
decision: Ask Saira whether Umar can take the amount owed (about $20,800 then, $16,111.98 after the 7 October Mercedes offset) now, labelled 'Director expense reimbursement'.
rationale: Repayment up to the amount owed is tax free; anything above it would become a shareholder loan under s.15(2).

subject: receipt-compression
title: Receipts sent to Saira

rationale: Umar asked to save space without reducing quality. Receipts went from 334 MB to 267 MB.

subject: lazer-t4a-sin

rationale: Otherwise CRA could add it to Umar's personal income and tax it twice. By 14 May 2026 Lazer had revoked the slip.

subject: lazer-t4a-sin
title: Lazer T4A carrying Umar's SIN
decision: Settled: Lazer revoked the 2025 T4A, so nothing is reported on Umar's personal return from it and nothing more is needed.
rationale: Recorded in the 14 May 2026 review. No written revocation notice is in the folder.

subject: donation-claim-2025

subject: t1135-2025

subject: capital-loss-2025

subject: contractor-payout-year-2024
title: Year of the January 2024 contractor payout

subject: mercedes-personal-use-offset
title: Charging Umar for personal use of the Mercedes
decision: Charge Umar the 20% personal share of 2026 Mercedes costs by offset against what the corporation owes him, with no cash moving: $7,119.48 for 2026 ($4,728.35 actual January to August, $2,391.13 estimated September to December), including $70.79, 20% of the 2 April service he paid. The part of the lease over the s.67.3 cap ($9,251.81 in 2026) is not charged to him. Replace the estimates with December actuals and book it at 31 December.
rationale: With 80% business use, 20% of the lease (on the capped amount), insurance and fuel is personal and cannot be deducted. Offsetting avoids a taxable benefit and needs no payment. Set out in a resolution that is drafted but not signed.
